messages:
noah.liu: Morning team  first-day snag. I can open Console staging but /admin/feature-flags returns 403. Need to flip a flag for a quick smoke canary and also check a service-account token for our CI job. Who's the right owner for staging FF admin and service-account provisioning? :wave:
taylor-sre: hey and welcome! FF admin is RBAC'd. For staging we do JIT role grants. Service accounts are handled separately by infra; normally create a short-lived svc account and mint a token. Which CI runner needs it?
noah.liu: it's the e2e-runner for my team's repo. I just need a temp FF toggle to validate traffic routing and a token that the runner can use in staging for one day.
jun.peopleops: welcome aboard Noah. For access flow: 1) create an ONB ticket with manager and purpose, 2) request `staging-ff-admin` JIT and a `staging-ci-svc` short-lived account. Sam approves platform elevations.
sam.platform: I can approve both. Noah, please open ONB-6239 and include manager + repo + time window. I'll sign once ticket exists. Also note we require token expiry <=24h for CI tokens unless there's a PR review.
noah.liu: ONB-6239 created, included @maria.tan as manager and details.
sam.platform: Approved. @onboarding-bot please grant staging FF admin and create svc acct `ci-e2e-noah` with 24h token.
onboarding-bot: Granted role `staging-ff-admin` to noah.liu until 2026-11-18T12:30:00Z. Created service account `ci-e2e-noah` with token expiring in 24h. Audit id: AUD-20261118-0042.
noah.liu: confirmed  I can access the FF admin UI and received the token. Quick question: is there a minimal checklist for canaries so I don't trigger rollbacks?
taylor-sre: short checklist: 1) start @1% for 10-15m, 2) smoke tests on critical flows, 3) monitor errors and p95, 4) step to 10% then 25% if stable. Auto-rollback triggers: +50% error rate or p95 +200ms. Preview targeting before enabling. Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/feature-flags/canary-runbook
jun.peopleops: keep ONB-6239 for the audit trail and tag the PR that depends on this token. If you need prod later, that's a separate security review.
noah.liu: thanks everyone  super fast. I'll run the smoke canary and post results here. Appreciate the help!
